title: yoga nidra
hook: at sunset the sun's rays gather back into the sun, and an Upanishad says the senses do the same at night

segments.voice: Yesterday, yoga nidra and the sankalpa, the short resolve said at the start and end. Which ordinary task did you name an intention for? Day one thousand twenty-four.

A student sits before a sage and asks a question about the body at night. When a person sleeps, what is it in them that sleeps? And what stays awake? The sage, Pippalada, answers with the evening sky. At sunset, he says, the rays of the sun all gather back into that one disc of light. At sunrise they spread out again. That's what happens to the senses every night. Today, the gathering in, and the strange instruction at the center of yoga nidra: touching the body with attention alone, one part at a time.
screen: `WHAT SLEEPS? WHAT STAYS AWAKE?` → `THE RAYS GATHER INTO THE SUN.` → `THE SENSES GATHER IN.`

segments.voice: In the Prashna Upanishad's fourth question, a student named Gargya asks this, and Pippalada's answer, in paraphrase, is this: as the rays of the setting sun become one in its disc of light, so in sleep all the senses become one in the mind, the highest of them. Then the person doesn't hear, doesn't see, doesn't smell or taste or touch, doesn't speak or take hold or move. And people say, he sleeps. Yet the breaths, the text says, keep watch in the city of the body, like fires kept burning in a house. So sleep, here, is a gathering in. Patanjali has a name for gathering in on purpose, while awake. In the second chapter of the Yoga Sutras he calls it pratyahara: the senses withdrawing from their objects and following the mind inward. The Gita gives the picture: a tortoise drawing in its limbs. Satyananda describes the practice as a way into pratyahara, and the main tool is a quick tour of the body called the rotation of awareness. The guide names a part, the right-hand thumb, the second finger, the third, the palm, the wrist, and the listener simply places attention there, without moving. Then the next part. Then the next. The sense of the body begins to quiet. The outside world thins. It looks like doing very little. But it's the senses being gathered back into the mind, the way the Upanishad saw the rays gathered into the sun, only this time on purpose.
screen: `THE SENSES BECOME ONE IN THE MIND.` · `THE BREATHS KEEP WATCH, LIKE FIRES.` · `PRATYAHARA: THE SENSES DRAWN IN.` · `ATTENTION TOURS THE BODY, PART BY PART.` · then, large: `THE RAYS GATHER INTO THE SUN.`

segments.voice: Lie down if you can, or sit back with eyes closed. Don't move; just let attention go where it's named. Right-hand thumb. Second finger. Third. Fourth. Fifth. Palm. Back of the hand. Wrist. Elbow. Shoulder. Right side of the chest. Right hip. Knee. Ankle. Right big toe. Now the whole right side, all at once. Then let attention rest on the breath, keeping watch, like a fire kept burning in a house. The bell holds the time.
Yoga nidra. The sleep of yoga, where the senses gather into the mind, like rays into the setting sun, this time on purpose.
Your line: yoga nidra. Today, once while you wait, close your eyes and move attention through one hand, thumb, each finger, palm, wrist, without moving it. Day one thousand twenty-four.

howItsDone: In guided yoga nidra, the teacher names parts of the body in a set order and listeners place attention on each without moving; teachers describe this rotation of awareness as a doorway to pratyahara, the withdrawal of the senses.

the senses gather into the mind, but the breaths keep watch in the body, like fires kept burning.

the listener places attention on each part without moving it.

fork.setup: the guide says: right-hand thumb. what do you do?
options: wiggle it, to be sure it's there.
fork.reveal: in the rotation of awareness you simply rest attention on the part named, then move on. The senses quiet, and attention watches them gather in.

original.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: pratyahara, the drawing in of the senses. In the Yoga Sutras, the limb of yoga before concentration.

trapdoor: what you thought: yoga nidra is just lying still and drifting off.
what it means: it gathers the senses into the mind on purpose, by touring the body with attention.
what a scholar hears: Prashna Upanishad 4.2–4.3 on sleep, and Yoga Sutra 2.54 on pratyahara.

sources.ref: Swami Satyananda Saraswati, Yoga Nidra (Bihar School of Yoga)

notes: Editor pass: cut the count 'built from six students' questions' (not in the cited verses) and named the questioner Gargya; rotation-to-pratyahara link attributed to Satyananda; carry changed, since 1015's carry already watched the light change at dusk; 'someone watching' lines trimmed so the witness stays tomorrow's angle.

Prashna Upanishad 4.2–4.3 paraphrased: rays gathering into the sun at sunset; senses becoming one in the mind (manas, 'the highest god'); 'he sleeps'; the pranas keeping watch in the city of the body like fires. Confirm. The voice says the Upanishad is 'built from six students' questions', which the text itself states in its opening; confirm.
The link between rotation of awareness and pratyahara follows Satyananda's own description; confirm wording.
The practice uses a shortened right-side rotation; the full sequence is longer.
